title: A binomial coefficient and power inequality
statement:
Let $n$, $s$, and $d$ be natural numbers satisfying $5s \le n$ and $d \le s$. Then
\[
  \binom{n}{s-d}\,(4n)^d \;\le\; \binom{n}{s}\,(5s)^d .
\]
replaced:
For natural numbers $n, s, d$ with $5s \leq n$ and $d \leq s$,
\[
  \binom{n}{s-d} \cdot (4n)^d \;\leq\; \binom{n}{s} \cdot (5s)^d .
\]
This is the purely combinatorial inequality used to convert the bad-restriction count
into the final $(10\,s\,w)^d$ form of the switching lemma.
